# JLang

> JLang is a small, open, bytecode-interpreted language for programming microcontrollers and learning how hardware works. 32-bit wrapping ints, first-class bit slicing, manual but checked memory, a desktop board simulator with virtual time, and interrupt-style event handlers. Implemented in portable C99.

## Tooling
- `jlang check FILE` compile only. Exit 0 = ok, 65 = compile error. Errors: `error (line L, col C): message` + source line + caret.
- `jlang run FILE [--emit EVENT]... [--pin N=0|1] [--analog N=0..4095] [--distance CM] [--answer TEXT] [--voice TEXT] [--kv K=V] [--heap BYTES] [--max-cycles N] [--stats]` run on the simulated board. Exit 70 = runtime error: `runtime error (line L): message` + call trace. Unfreed memory is reported at exit as `leak: ...` on stderr.
- More `run` options: `--temperature C` (simulated I2C sensor), `--for SECONDS` (how long timers run, default 10), `--vcd FILE` (every pin as a VCD waveform for GTKWave), `--panel WxH`, `--realtime`.
- `jlang xray FILE` trace every instruction. `jlang dis FILE` print bytecode. `jlang new NAME` scaffold a project.
- `jlang wcet FILE [--mhz N]` worst-case cycles of the script and each `on` handler from the machine code (only `for i in A..B` with constant bounds is bounded). `jlang svd CHIP.svd [--only GPIO,UART0.FIFO] [-o FILE]` prints registers as consts: NAME (address), NAME_HI/NAME_LO (bit field), NAME_BIT (one bit).

## Syntax
- No semicolons. Blocks `{ }`. Conditions without parentheses. Comments `//` and `/* */`.
- `let x = 1` (top level = global, in a block = local). `let y` is nil.
- `fn name(a, b) { return a + b }` top level only. Functions are values.
- `if c { } else if d { } else { }`, `match x { 0 => { } 1, 2 => { } _ => { } }`, `while c { }`, `for i in 0..n { }` (end exclusive), `break`, `continue`.
- `on EVENT { }` top level only; runs when the host fires EVENT (`--emit EVENT` or `emit("EVENT")`). On ESP32, BOOT fires `button`, `button_hold` (>= 600 ms) and `button_release`.
- `every 500ms { }` repeats, `after 2s { }` runs once; top level only; they start counting when the line runs and run after the top level finishes. `stop_timer()` inside one stops it. Time literals: `500ms` = 500, `2s` = 2000 (ints, ms). Like setInterval/setTimeout; only one handler or timer runs at a time.
- `const NAME = 42` top level only: a compile-time number (int literal, negative literal or another const), inlined, takes no memory, can't be assigned.
- `struct Point { x, y }` top level only (fields on lines or comma separated). `Point { x: 1, y: 2 }` heap struct, every field required, any order. `p.x`, `p.x = 3`, `p.x += 1`. `free(p)`. Passed by reference; `==` is identity; 8 bytes per field; memmap shows field offsets. Not in native code.
- Assignment is a statement only: `x = 1`, `x += 1` (also -= *= /= %= &= |= ^= <<= >>=), `buf[i] = v`, `reg[3] = 1`, `reg[7..4] = 5`. Never inside an expression.

## Types
- nil, bool, int (32-bit signed, wraps; no floats), str (read-only bytes), buf (heap bytes), array (heap list of any values), struct (heap, named fields), fn, built-in.
- Literals: `123`, `1_000`, `0xFF`, `0b1010`, `'A'` (=65), `"text\n"` (escapes \n \t \r \0 \\ \" \' \xHH), `true`, `false`, `nil`.
- Truthiness: nil, false, 0 are false; everything else true.

## Operators (low to high precedence)
`||` `&&` (short-circuit, give bool) · `==` `!=` · `<` `<=` `>` `>=` (ints) · `|` · `^` · `&` · `<<` `>>` (0..31, >> arithmetic) · `+` `-` · `*` `/` `%` (truncate toward zero; /0 is an error) · unary `-` `!` `~` · call `f()`, index `x[i]`, bit range `x[hi..lo]`.
NOTE: bitwise binds tighter than comparison: `x & 1 == 0` is `(x & 1) == 0`. `+` with a str on either side joins as text (numbers printed like print) into a NEW HEAP str that must be freed; in a chain "a" + b + c the intermediate strings are freed automatically. `s += x` leaks the old string. `fmt(fmt, ...)` -> heap str with printf placeholders.

## Bits
- `x[i]` on an int reads bit i (0..31) as 0/1. `x[hi..lo]` reads bits hi down to lo.
- On a variable: `x[i] = 0|1|true|false`, `x[hi..lo] = v` (error if v doesn't fit), `x[i] ^= 1`.
- `u8(v)` `i8(v)` `u16(v)` `i16(v)` keep the low bits.

## Memory
- `alloc(n)` returns a zeroed buf of n bytes; every alloc needs exactly one `free(buf)`.
- `buf[i]` reads/writes a byte 0..255 (storing outside 0..255 is an error; use u8()).
- `len(x)` for buf/str. `read16/read32(buf, off)`, `write16/write32(buf, off, v)` are little-endian.
- Arrays: `[1, 2, "x"]` (trailing comma ok), `array(n)` (n zeros), `array(n, v)`; `a[i]`, `a[i] = v`, `a[i] += 1`, nested `g[y][x] = 1`; `len(a)` items; `free(a)`; `==` is identity. 8 bytes per item on the heap. Not in native code.
- Use after free, double free, out-of-bounds and leaks are detected and reported with line numbers. A leak is a heap block nothing refers to at exit; blocks still referenced by globals are not reported.
- Strings returned by built-ins such as `ask()`, `slice()`, `trim()` and `kv_get()` are on the heap and must be freed. String literals must not be freed.
- `mem()` prints heap stats, `memmap()` prints the block layout.

## Built-ins
stop_timer() · random(lo, hi) inclusive · map(v, a, b, c, d) rescale · clamp(v, lo, hi) · rgb(r, g, b) -> 0xRRGGBB · print(...) · fmt(fmt, ...) -> heap str · printf(fmt, ...) placeholders {} {d} {x} {b} {c} with optional width e.g. {x2} {b8} {d5}, {d05} pads with zeros, `{{ }}` literal braces, no automatic newline · contains(s, sub) -> bool · starts_with(s, pre) -> bool · ends_with(s, suf) -> bool · slice(s, start, end) -> heap str · trim(s) -> heap str · alloc(n) · free(x) (buf, array, heap str) · len(x) · array(n[, v]) · read16 read32 write16 write32 · u8 i8 u16 i16 · mem() · memmap() · cycles() · assert(cond, msg) · emit(name)

## Board built-ins (simulated on desktop, real on device)
pin_mode(pin, "out"|"in"|"in_pullup") · pin_write(pin, 0|1) (pin must be "out") · pin_read(pin) (pin must be an input) · delay(ms) (virtual time) · millis() · capture() -> buf (free it) · record(ms) -> audio buf (sim: --voice TEXT, free it) · ask(photo_or_nil, prompt_or_audio[, instruction]) -> str (free it) · speak(text, lang="en") · chime("ready"|"working"|"error") · kv_set(key, val) · kv_get(key[, default]) -> heap str or nil (free if non-nil) · kv_del(key) -> bool
Parts (set up the pin themselves, no pin_mode needed): turn_on(pin) · turn_off(pin) · toggle(pin) · brightness(pin, 0..100) PWM · color(pin, "red"|0xRRGGBB) WS2812 LED · color_at(pin, n, colour) strip LED n 0..63 · tone(pin, hz|"C#5"|"rest", ms) blocks for ms · beep(pin) · servo(pin, 0..180) · pressed(pin) -> bool, true once per press of a button to ground, debounced · analog(pin) -> 0..4095 (sim: --analog N=V, default 2048) · distance(trig, echo) -> cm or -1 (sim: --distance CM, default 100). Colour names: red green blue yellow cyan magenta orange purple pink white warm off. These are VM-only: compile errors in native code.

LED panel (sim 60x7, --panel WxH): led(x, y, colour) sets a frame pixel, off-panel ignored · led_clear() · led_show() sends the frame (records millis; browser plays frames at those times) · led_text(text|number, x, y, colour) 5x7 font, 6 px advance, returns next x · led_width() · led_height() · led_size() -> [w, h] array, free it · rgb(r, g, b). led/led_clear/led_show/led_width/led_height/rgb also work in native code.

I2C and SPI: i2c_scan() -> array of addresses (free it) · i2c_write(addr, byte, ...) first byte is usually a register · i2c_read(addr, reg) -> byte · i2c_read16(addr, reg) -> 16-bit, high byte first · spi_write(cs, byte, ...) · spi_transfer(cs, byte) -> byte received. Simulated bus: TMP102 at 0x48 (reg 0: temperature as 12 bits of 1/16 C in the top bits; C = (i2c_read16(0x48, 0) >> 4) / 16), MPU-6050 at 0x68 (WHO_AM_I 0x75 = 0x68; starts asleep, i2c_write(0x68, 0x6B, 0) wakes it; accel z 0x3F reads 16384 = 1 g), OLED at 0x3C. Unknown addresses are an error. SPI reads 0xFF in the simulator. VM-only.

## Native code (RISC-V)
- `jlang emu FILE [--emit EVENT] [--asm] [--listing]` compiles to RV32IM and runs on the built-in emulator. `jlang build FILE -o out.s` writes assembly for a real board, which links with a C file implementing boards/jl_hal.h. `jlang asm FILE.s` assembles and runs hand-written assembly.
- Native code is experimental: a program either behaves exactly as on the VM or is a compile error. It supports ints, bools, nil, string literals and string variables, functions (also as values), loops, `match`, bits and slices, events, const, print/printf, pins, delay/millis, u8/i8/u16/i16, assert, cycles(), the LED panel. Functions can only be given numbers and functions and can only return numbers or bools. Arithmetic on bool/nil/str is a compile error; values of different types compare unequal; bool/str/fn variables keep their type. No heap: alloc/free/len/read32/write32, arrays, structs, fmt, string +, string indexing, string helpers, mem/memmap, capture/record/ask/speak/chime, kv_*, timers, part built-ins and I2C/SPI are compile errors.
- `jlang emu FILE --pipeline [ROWS]` prints a 5-stage pipeline diagram (F D X M W, forwarding, 1-cycle load-use stall, 2 flushed after a taken branch) and CPI for the whole run.
- `mmio_read32(addr)`, `mmio_write32(addr, v)`, `mmio_read8`, `mmio_write8` access hardware registers (also simulated by `jlang run`). Simulated board map: UART 0x10000000 (write a byte), GPIO_DIR 0x10001000, GPIO_PULL 0x10001004, GPIO_OUT 0x10001008, GPIO_IN 0x1000100C, TIMER_MS 0x10002000, TIMER_WAIT 0x10002004.
- `asm("li t0, 1; addi t0, t0, 2")` inserts RISC-V instructions (native only; `;` separates instructions; the string must be a literal). Registers s0, s1 and sp belong to JLang and must be restored.
- Native runtime errors print `runtime error (line L): message` and stop the program.

## Example
```
let LED = 2
pin_mode(LED, "out")
let status = 0
status[7..4] = 0b1010
on button {
    let photo = capture()
    let answer = ask(photo, "What bus is this?")
    free(photo)
    speak(answer, "en")
    free(answer)
    pin_write(LED, 1)
}
```
